dct_description_sm: This study aims to provide clues about factors such as changing climate and human-caused releases on Hg deposition in the Arctic by using Hg isotope measurements. The objectives were to 1) determine if and how Hg isotopic signatures in terrestrial Arctic snow and ice vary at different temporal and spatial scales, 2) compare Hg isotopic composition in ice core samples from periods with high/low extremes in temperature and sea ice cover to discriminate between climatic changes and anthropogenic changes, and 3) if possible, identify Hg sources to the Arctic and how they change through time as well as how they are affected by climate variations.
dct_title_s: Spatial and temporal variations of mercury (Hg) isotope ratios in ice cores across the Canadian Arctic
